newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Labour party to pick new leader in June.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Labour party to pick new leader in June.

text.p: Israel's main opposition Labour party announced on Thursday it will choose a new leader on June 3 to replace former prime minister Shimon Peres, who has announced he will not contest the next national election.

"We took a first step forward today towards renewal and focusing on our true rival, the Likud and the government," former foreign minister Ehud Barak said after the party's central committee set the internal election date.
Barak, an ex-army chief, is the leading contender to succeed Peres.

"Shimon made a choice -- and announced it more than a month ago -- that he does not intend to run (in national elections) in the year 2000 or even participate in the (Labour) primaries in the summer," Barak told reporters.
Peres, 73, lost last May's election for prime minister to Likud chief Benjamin Netanyahu by only 29,000 votes. He will continue to head Labour until a new leader is picked.

Barak said that under a "gentlemen's agreement" he reached with Peres, the former prime minister will have final say -- only during 1997 -- on whether Labour would join a national unity government if invited to do so by Likud.
